article.headline: Games To Watch: Unbeaten Center Hill and Ripley collide; Harrison Central faces West Harrison
article.html:
An unbeaten start will be tested Thursday night in Ripley, where Center Hill brings a 4-0 boys basketball record to a Tigers team that is 3-0. On the Coast, Harrison Central takes a perfect 6-0 boys soccer record to West Harrison, which has lost only once in a 7-1-1 opening.

Those meetings lead this November 19 Games To Watch selection, with basketball doubleheaders in Ripley and Southaven and soccer doubleheaders at Center Hill and West Harrison. All start times below are Central Standard Time and were checked before publication.

Center Hill at Ripley: perfect boys records, evenly matched girls starts

The 7 p.m. boys game pairs two teams that have yet to take a reported loss. Center Hill enters 4-0 and Ripley 3-0, making this a direct test of both unbeaten openings. Center Hill lists Cardale Manuel at 18.5 points per game, giving the Mustangs a proven scoring option for the road test. The game is listed as nonconference.

The girls game tips at 6 p.m. with both teams at 3-1. Their matching records give the opener a different balance from the unbeaten boys meeting: either the Mustangs or Tigers can leave with a fourth victory and only one loss.

For the results that preceded this matchup, see our Tuesday recap covering Ripley and Center Hill.

Harrison Central at West Harrison: winning starts meet in district soccer

Harrison Central puts its 6-0 boys record on the line in the 7 p.m. match at West Harrison. The Hurricanes enter 7-1-1, giving the Red Rebels an opponent that has already built a substantial winning record of its own. The match is listed as a conference contest, adding district significance to the effort to stay unbeaten.

The girls match starts at 5:30 p.m.. West Harrison is 7-1, while Harrison Central is 3-4-1. That makes the opener an opportunity for the Red Rebels to challenge a strong early record on the road; the Hurricanes can protect their winning start in another fixture listed as a conference match.

South Panola at Southaven: unbeaten teams on opposite sides of the doubleheader

South Panola brings the unbeaten girls team into the 6 p.m. opener. The Tigers are 5-0 and Southaven is 2-2. It is also a rematch: South Panola won the November 10 meeting 54-40. Southaven can move above the break-even mark by reversing that result, while South Panola has an opportunity to add another victory against the Chargers.

The roles reverse in the 7:30 p.m. boys game: Southaven is 2-0, while South Panola is looking for its first reported win after a 0-5 start. The Chargers have the perfect record to protect, and the Tigers have a chance to change the direction of their opening stretch. Both basketball games are listed as nonconference.

Oxford at Center Hill: Chargers take winning soccer records on the road

Oxford’s girls enter the 5:30 p.m. match at 4-1 against a Center Hill team listed at 2-3. The Chargers can build on a start with only one defeat, while the Mustangs can get back to an even record by winning at home.

The 7 p.m. boys match brings together two winning records: Oxford is 3-1-1 and Center Hill is 4-2. Neither team is unbeaten, but each has more wins than losses to defend in a nonconference meeting. With both Oxford squads traveling to Olive Branch, the doubleheader offers a useful comparison of how their early form holds up away from home.
